instruction: Open the Colab notebook at https://colab.research.google.com/drive/1JMLa53HDuA-i7ZBmqV7ZnA3c_fvtXnx- in Chrome (already open), view the Python code cells, extract all method names from all classes (methods starting with 'def' inside class definitions), and save them to 'method_names.txt' in the Home directory with one method name per line. Only include methods defined inside classes, not module-level functions.

metadata.explanation: Task requires opening a Colab notebook in Chrome, viewing Python code cells, and extracting method names from class definitions. The notebook contains PyTorch neural network classes with methods like __init__, forward, generate, etc. Evaluator verifies: (1) file contains valid Python method names (one per line), (2) at least 10 methods are listed, (3) names follow method naming conventions (snake_case or dunder methods, not PascalCase class names), (4) contains common PyTorch patterns like __init__ and forward, (5) at least 8 unique method names, (6) includes ground truth method names from typical GPT implementations. The Colab is already open in Chrome via preconfig.

notebook_context.rationale_for_min_methods_10: Typical GPT implementation has 5+ classes with 2+ methods each (__init__, forward), resulting in 10+ total method names when extracted
notebook_context.rationale_for_min_unique_8: With 5+ classes each having unique __init__ and forward, plus helper methods, expect at least 8 unique method names (accounting for duplicates of __init__ and forward)

metadata.scoring_breakdown: Weighted scoring: 25% for method count (min 10), 20% for unique methods (min 8), 20% for PyTorch patterns (__init__ and forward present), 35% for ground truth overlap (at least 50% of ground truth method names must match). Partial credit enabled for each component.
metadata.verification_limitations: Cannot directly verify methods were extracted from Colab vs other sources, but evaluator validates: (1) file format and valid Python identifiers, (2) method count and uniqueness thresholds, (3) presence of expected ground truth method names from GPT implementations, (4) PyTorch patterns like __init__ and forward. Chrome preconfig ensures Colab is accessible to agent.

llm_judge_reasons: Critical: Cannot verify extraction source. Instruction requires extracting from specific Colab URL (https://colab.research.google.com/drive/1JMLa53HDuA-i7ZBmqV7ZnA3c_fvtXnx-), but evaluator only checks file content. Agent could extract from any Python file and pass.

Critical: Cannot distinguish class methods from module-level functions. Instruction explicitly requires 'methods starting with def inside class definitions, not module-level functions', but getter at class_method_names__d8f1c2a9.py:42-69 only filters PascalCase and validates identifiers - cannot verify methods are from classes.

Significant: Ground truth not from actual Colab. The ground_truth_method_names list (__init__, forward, generate, etc.) is based on assumptions about 'typical GPT implementations' (see metadata.notebook_context.rationale_for_min_methods_10), not extracted from the actual Colab notebook URL.

Significant: Incomplete coverage of instruction requirement. Core requirement is 'extract from Colab code cells', but evaluator has no mechanism to verify this. Only validates: file exists, contains valid identifiers, meets count thresholds, contains expected patterns.

Logic limitation: Getter filtering logic (class_method_names__d8f1c2a9.py:57-59) filters PascalCase to remove 'class names', but this heuristic is weak - it would accept module-level snake_case functions as if they were class methods.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Access the actual Colab notebook URL to extract ground truth: exact method names, exact class structure, exact counts. Update expected.rules.ground_truth_method_names with verified data from the notebook.
Strengthen verification by adding exact method name matching. Replace heuristic thresholds (min_methods=10, min_unique_names=8) with exact expected method names from ground truth analysis.
Consider adding Chrome accessibility tree verification in postconfig to check if agent interacted with the Colab URL (e.g., check active tab contains 'colab.research.google.com').
Alternative: Simplify instruction to remove unverifiable requirement. Change to 'extract method names from a Python code file' without specifying Colab source, making the task fully verifiable.
If keeping Colab requirement, document this as a limitation: evaluator verifies format and content quality but cannot verify extraction source (Colab vs other Python files).
